question: A 35-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 40 minutes after spilling hot oil over himself in a kitchen accident. Examination shows multiple tense blisters over the abdomen, anterior chest, and anterior and posterior aspects of the right upper extremity and right thigh. On deroofing the blisters, the skin underneath is tender, mottled, and does not blanch with pressure. The skin over the left thigh is tender, erythematous, and shows quick capillary refill after blanching with pressure. Which of the following most closely approximates the body surface area affected by 2nd-degree burns in this patient?
